{{short description|Croatian theoretical physicist}}
'''Vladimir Jurko Glaser''' (21 April 1924 – 22 January 1984) was a [[Croatia]]n [[theoretical physicist]] working on [[quantum field theory]] and the canonization of the analytic [[S-matrix]].

==Biography==
Glaser was born in [[Gorizia]], [[Italy]]. His father, Vladimir Glaser, was a prominent [[Slovenes|Slovene]] lawyer and minority rights activist. His mother, Ana née Besednjak, was the sister of the politician [[Engelbert Besednjak]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.slovenska-biografija.si/oseba/sbi1009970/ | title=Glaser, Vladimir (1894–1975) - Slovenska biografija }}</ref> His paternal aunt Eleonora (Lola) was married to the famous neurologist [[Constantin von Economo]].<ref>Amalija Maček et al., "O strukturi tržaškega meščanstva v 19. in začetku 20. stoletja. Prikaz na primeru družinske zgodovine Sergija Vilfana". Kronika 67 (2019), p. 564</ref>

The family fled to Yugoslavia in 1929, first to [[Maribor]], then to [[Belgrade]], [[Odžaci]] and finally to [[Zagreb]] in 1941. He graduated [[physics]] from the [[University of Zagreb]] in 1949 and later was attending seminar of [[Werner Heisenberg]] (1951-52) at [[Göttingen]]. Based on work carried out in [[Göttingen]] under [[Werner Heisenberg|Heisenberg]] he received a doctorate degree from the [[University of Zagreb]]. Being a part of [[Werner Heisenberg|Heisenberg's]] group at [[Göttingen]] he later worked with many famous physicists such as [[Harry Lehmann]], [[Wolfhart Zimmermann]] (on extensions of [[LSZ reduction formula|LSZ formalism]]) and [[Walter Thirring]].<ref>{{cite journal |author1=V. Glaser |author2=H. Lehmann |author3=W. Zimmermann | title=Field operators and retarded functions | journal=Il Nuovo Cimento | year=1957 | volume=6 | issue=5 | pages=1122–1128| doi=10.1007/BF02747395 | bibcode=1957NCim....6.1122G | s2cid=119732435 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | author=Walter Thirring | title=The Joy of Discovery: Great Encounters Along the Way | publisher=University of Vienna, Austria & CERN, Switzerland | year=2010}}</ref> From 1955 to 1957 he was head of the Department of Theoretical Physics at the [[Ruđer Bošković Institute]] in [[Zagreb]]. In 1957 he found a [[permanent employment]] at the Department  of Theoretical  Physics of [[CERN]], [[Geneva]]. He died in [[Geneva]].<ref name="Bio1"/><ref name="Bio2"/>

In 1955, he published one of the first monographs on [[quantum electrodynamics]], ''Kovarijantna kvantna elektrodinamika'' (in [[Croatian language|Croatian]]).<ref>{{cite book | author=Vladimir Glaser | title=Kovarijantna kvantna elektrodinamika | publisher=Yugoslav Academy of Arts and Sciences | year=1955}}</ref> With [[French people|French]] physicists [[Jacques Bros]] and [[Henri Epstein]] he worked on setting up analyticity properties required for the use of dispersion relations in high energy collisions.<ref name="Bio1"/> [[Henri Epstein|Epstein]], Glaser and [[Arthur Jaffe]] proved  that (Wightman) quantum fields can necessarily have negative energy density values.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=H. Epstein |author2=V. Glaser |author3=A. Jaffe | title=Nonpositivity of the Energy Density in Quantized Field Theories | journal=Nuovo Cimento | year=1965 | volume=36 | issue=3 | pages=1016–1022| doi=10.1007/BF02749799 | bibcode=1965NCim...36.1016E | s2cid=120375522 }}</ref> Together with [[Henri Epstein]], he found a new approach to [[renormalization]] theory called [[causal perturbation theory]], where [[ultraviolet divergence]]s are avoided in the calculation of [[Feynman diagrams]] by using mathematically well-defined quantities only.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Epstein, H |author2=Jurko, Vladimir Glaser | title=The role of locality in perturbation theory | journal=Annales de l'Institut Henri Poincaré A| year=1973 | volume=19 | issue=3 | pages=211–295}}</ref>
